_comment: Retirements RATIFIED but not yet EXECUTED (or half-executed). A task listed here is registered with enabled:false ONLY because its retirement is still in flight -- it is NOT paused, and any fleet-wide resume that re-enables it silently reverses a ratified decision. pause-resume-guard.py (native, off-fleet, every 6h) alarms if a listed id is found enabled:true on its named fleet; register-scheduled-task v2.14 requires every bulk resume to carve these ids out. Remove an entry in the same pass that actually completes its retirement. This file is a plain state register consulted by a guard -- it is NOT a scheduler registry, and writing to it retires nothing by itself (Rule 2 is unaffected).

_completed.lesson: ARCHIVE-FIRST-DELETE-SECOND is correct for the FILE, but it opens a resurrection window that lasts until the REGISTRY row is dropped. Any half-executed retirement left in that window will re-materialise its own spec folder and re-alarm every guard run. Close both steps in the same pass where the surface allows it; where it does not, this register plus pause-resume-guard.py is what keeps the window observable.
